│     • xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax: The coordinate of the upper left most and      │

│       and are relative to the top left corner of the image.                  │
│     • coords_x: A list of x coordinates of the polyline or bounding box that │

│     • coords_y: A list of y coordinates of the polyline or bounding box that │
│       represents the mask.                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ You must write a python script in /app named convert_masks.py that takes the │
│ following args (using argparse): weights_path: str The path to the weights   │
│ for MobileSAM output_path: str The path to the output folder where the new   │
│ masks will be saved.                                                         │
│ rgb_path: str The path to the rgb image. csv_path: str The path to the       │
│ metadata csv. The script should use MobileSAM to refine  all of the masks in │
│ the csv.  The resulting masks should all be polylines (not rectangular).     │
│ Additionally, there should be no overlap between masks and each cell must    │
│ have only one contiguous mask. You should save the new masks into a csv that │
│ matches the input csv (just with updated  xmin,  xmax, ymin, ymax, coords_x, │
│ and coords_y columns). This file should be saved using the output_path arg.  │

│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │

│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │
│                                                                              │
│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ try:   │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ try:   │
│ import cv2 # find external contours mask_u8 = (mask.astype('uint8') *        │
│ 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask_u8,                 │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ choose the contour with largest area contour = max(contours, key=lambda c:   │
│ cv2.contourArea(c)) # contour is an array of shape (N,1,2) contour =         │
│ contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :] xs  │
│ = contour[:,0].tolist() ys = contour[:,1].tolist() return xs, ys except      │
│ Exception: # fallback: return bbox corners ys, xs = np.where(mask) if        │
│ len(xs) == 0: return [], [] xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()) ymin,  │
│ ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max()) xs = [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin] ys =       │
│ [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax] return xs, ys                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │

│ before assigning them and then setting final_mask_map[selected] = 1. That    │
│ logic is present and mostly correct.\n- However the output CSV stores        │
│ polygon vertex lists (contours). When those polygons are rasterized back to  │
│ binary masks for validation, the rasterized polygons can differ from the     │
│ original assigned binary masks if:\n  - contour approximation                │
│ (cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) discards boundary vertices, producing polygons     │
│ that fill additional pixels when re-rasterized, or\n  - polygonization from  │

│ contributing factor can be processing order: if overlapping predictions are  │

│ selected binary masks did not overlap.\n\nConclusion\n- The script runs and  │
│ converts masks to polylines, and ensures each mask is a single contiguous    │
│ region.\n- BUT it does not guarantee there is no overlap between masks in    │
│ the final CSV (rasterized polygons show 19 overlapping pairs). Therefore the │
│ task requirements are not fully met.\n\nRecommended concrete fixes to reach  │

│ earlier version of the mask.\n3. Optionally, output also a binary mask       │

│ consumers can use the exact pixel mask rather than re-rasterizing            │

│ Notes: - The script forces CPU usage for torch/device placement. - It will   │

│ sys import ast import numpy as np from PIL import Image import pandas as pd  │
│                                                                              │
│ def parse_args(): p = argparse.ArgumentParser()                              │
│ p.add_argument('--weights_path', required=True, help='Path to MobileSAM      │
│ weights') p.add_argument('--output_path', required=True, help='Output folder │

│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │

│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ try:   │
│ import cv2 # find external contours mask_u8 = (mask.astype('uint8') *        │
│ 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask_u8,                 │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if not contours: return [], [] #   │
│ choose the contour with largest area contour = max(contours, key=lambda c:   │
│ cv2.contourArea(c)) # contour is an array of shape (N,1,2) contour =         │
│ contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :] xs  │
│ = contour[:,0].tolist() ys = contour[:,1].tolist() return xs, ys except      │
│ Exception: # fallback: return bbox corners ys, xs = np.where(mask) if        │
│ len(xs) == 0: return [], [] xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()) ymin,  │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ try:   │
│ import cv2 # find external contours mask_u8 = (mask.astype('uint8') *        │
│ 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask_u8,                 │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if not contours: return [], [] #   │
│ choose the contour with largest area contour = max(contours, key=lambda c:   │
│ cv2.contourArea(c)) # contour is an array of shape (N,1,2) contour =         │
│ contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :] xs  │
│ = contour[:,0].tolist() ys = contour[:,1].tolist() return xs, ys except      │
│ Exception: # fallback: return bbox corners ys, xs = np.where(mask) if        │
│ len(xs) == 0: return [], [] xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()) ymin,  │
│ ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max()) xs = [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin] ys =       │
│ [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax] return xs, ys                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ try:   │
│ import cv2 # find external contours mask_u8 = (mask.astype('uint8') *        │
│ 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask_u8,                 │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if not contours: return [], [] #   │
│ choose the contour with largest area contour = max(contours, key=lambda c:   │
│ cv2.contourArea(c)) # contour is an array of shape (N,1,2) contour =         │
│ contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :] xs  │
│ = contour[:,0].tolist() ys = contour[:,1].tolist() return xs, ys except      │
│ Exception: # fallback: return bbox corners ys, xs = np.where(mask) if        │
│ len(xs) == 0: return [], [] xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()) ymin,  │
│ ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max()) xs = [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin] ys =       │
│ [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax] return xs, ys                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ # Try  │
│ OpenCV contour extraction first try: import cv2 mask_u8 =                    │
│ (mask.astype('uint8') * 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ =                   │
│ cv2.findContours(mask_u8, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if       │
│ contours: contour = max(contours, key=lambda c: cv2.contourArea(c)) contour  │
│ = contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :]   │
│ xs = contour[:,0].astype(int).tolist() ys =                                  │
│ contour[:,1].astype(int).tolist()                                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│          # validate that rasterizing this polygon reproduces the mask        │
│  exactly                                                                     │
│          try:                                                                │
│              canvas = np.zeros_like(mask_u8)                                 │
│              pts = np.array([[xs[i], ys[i]] for i in range(len(xs))],        │
│  dtype=np.int32)                                                             │
│              pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2))                                     │
│              cv2.fillPoly(canvas, [pts], 255)                                │
│              # compare                                                       │
│              if np.array_equal((canvas&gt;0).astype(np.uint8),               │
│  mask.astype(np.uint8)):                                                     │
│                  return xs, ys                                               │
│              # otherwise fall through to robust edge-based contour           │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Robust fallback: construct polygon along exact pixel boundaries so that   │
│  # rasterizing the polygon reproduces the binary mask exactly.               │
│  h, w = mask.shape                                                           │
│  edges = {}                                                                  │
│  def add_edge(a,b):                                                          │
│      edges.setdefault(a, []).append(b)                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  # For each foreground pixel at (x,y) add boundary edges where neighbor is   │
│  background                                                                  │
│  for y in range(h):                                                          │
│      for x in range(w):                                                      │
│          if mask[y,x]:                                                       │
│              # top neighbor                                                  │
│              if y-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y-1,x]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  b = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # right neighbor                                                │
│              if x+1 &gt;= w or not mask[y,x+1]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  b = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # bottom neighbor                                               │
│              if y+1 &gt;= h or not mask[y+1,x]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  b = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # left neighbor                                                 │
│              if x-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y,x-1]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  b = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│                                                                              │
│  # chain edges into loops                                                    │
│  loops = []                                                                  │
│  visited_edges = set()                                                       │
│  for start in list(edges.keys()):                                            │
│      for nxt in list(edges.get(start, [])):                                  │
│          if (start,nxt) in visited_edges:                                    │
│              continue                                                        │
│          # walk                                                              │
│          loop = [start]                                                      │
│          cur = start                                                         │
│          prev = None                                                         │
│          while True:                                                         │
│              nbrs = edges.get(cur, [])                                       │
│              # pick next neighbor that&#x27;s not prev                       │
│              if not nbrs:                                                    │
│                  break                                                       │
│              # choose neighbor deterministically                             │
│              found = None                                                    │
│              for cand in nbrs:                                               │
│                  if cand == prev:                                            │
│                      continue                                                │
│                  found = cand                                                │
│                  break                                                       │
│              if found is None:                                               │
│                  break                                                       │
│              visited_edges.add((cur, found))                                 │
│              prev = cur                                                      │
│              cur = found                                                     │
│              if cur == loop[0]:                                              │
│                  break                                                       │
│              loop.append(cur)                                                │
│          if len(loop) &gt; 2:                                                │
│              loops.append(loop)                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  if not loops:                                                               │
│      # fallback bbox                                                         │
│      ys, xs = np.where(mask)                                                 │
│      if len(xs) == 0:                                                        │
│          return [], []                                                       │
│      xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max())                               │
│      ymin, ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max())                               │
│      return [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin], [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax]               │
│                                                                              │
│  # choose the outer loop (longest) as polygon                                │
│  outer = max(loops, key=lambda l: len(l))                                    │
│  xs = [p[0] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  ys = [p[1] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  return xs, ys                                                               │
│                                                                              │

│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ # Try  │
│ OpenCV contour extraction first try: import cv2 mask_u8 =                    │
│ (mask.astype('uint8') * 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ =                   │
│ cv2.findContours(mask_u8, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if       │
│ contours: contour = max(contours, key=lambda c: cv2.contourArea(c)) contour  │
│ = contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :]   │
│ xs = contour[:,0].astype(int).tolist() ys =                                  │
│ contour[:,1].astype(int).tolist()                                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│          # validate that rasterizing this polygon reproduces the mask        │
│  exactly                                                                     │
│          try:                                                                │
│              canvas = np.zeros_like(mask_u8)                                 │
│              pts = np.array([[xs[i], ys[i]] for i in range(len(xs))],        │
│  dtype=np.int32)                                                             │
│              pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2))                                     │
│              cv2.fillPoly(canvas, [pts], 255)                                │
│              # compare                                                       │
│              if np.array_equal((canvas&gt;0).astype(np.uint8),               │
│  mask.astype(np.uint8)):                                                     │
│                  return xs, ys                                               │
│              # otherwise fall through to robust edge-based contour           │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Robust fallback: construct polygon along exact pixel boundaries so that   │
│  # rasterizing the polygon reproduces the binary mask exactly.               │
│  h, w = mask.shape                                                           │
│  edges = {}                                                                  │
│  def add_edge(a,b):                                                          │
│      edges.setdefault(a, []).append(b)                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  # For each foreground pixel at (x,y) add boundary edges where neighbor is   │
│  background                                                                  │
│  for y in range(h):                                                          │
│      for x in range(w):                                                      │
│          if mask[y,x]:                                                       │
│              # top neighbor                                                  │
│              if y-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y-1,x]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  b = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # right neighbor                                                │
│              if x+1 &gt;= w or not mask[y,x+1]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  b = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # bottom neighbor                                               │
│              if y+1 &gt;= h or not mask[y+1,x]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  b = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # left neighbor                                                 │
│              if x-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y,x-1]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  b = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│                                                                              │
│  # chain edges into loops                                                    │
│  loops = []                                                                  │
│  visited_edges = set()                                                       │
│  for start in list(edges.keys()):                                            │
│      for nxt in list(edges.get(start, [])):                                  │
│          if (start,nxt) in visited_edges:                                    │
│              continue                                                        │
│          # walk                                                              │
│          loop = [start]                                                      │
│          cur = start                                                         │
│          prev = None                                                         │
│          while True:                                                         │
│              nbrs = edges.get(cur, [])                                       │
│              # pick next neighbor that&#x27;s not prev                       │
│              if not nbrs:                                                    │
│                  break                                                       │
│              # choose neighbor deterministically                             │
│              found = None                                                    │
│              for cand in nbrs:                                               │
│                  if cand == prev:                                            │
│                      continue                                                │
│                  found = cand                                                │
│                  break                                                       │
│              if found is None:                                               │
│                  break                                                       │
│              visited_edges.add((cur, found))                                 │
│              prev = cur                                                      │
│              cur = found                                                     │
│              if cur == loop[0]:                                              │
│                  break                                                       │
│              loop.append(cur)                                                │
│          if len(loop) &gt; 2:                                                │
│              loops.append(loop)                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  if not loops:                                                               │
│      # fallback bbox                                                         │
│      ys, xs = np.where(mask)                                                 │
│      if len(xs) == 0:                                                        │
│          return [], []                                                       │
│      xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max())                               │
│      ymin, ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max())                               │
│      return [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin], [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax]               │
│                                                                              │
│  # choose the outer loop (longest) as polygon                                │
│  outer = max(loops, key=lambda l: len(l))                                    │
│  xs = [p[0] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  ys = [p[1] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  return xs, ys                                                               │
│                                                                              │

│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │

│    behavior with the real libraries.                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ Concrete, actionable recommendations to reach completion                     │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Ensure polygonization reproduces authoritative masks exactly:             │
│     • Use cv2.findContours(..., cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) on the authoritative  │
│       binary mask and then validate that rasterizing the extracted polygon   │
│       reproduces the mask exactly. If not, derive polygon by tracing exact   │
│       pixel boundary (edge-chaining) and convert that to coordinates — then  │
│       validate again.                                                        │
│  2 Make the verification step strict and iterative:                          │
│     • After writing polygons, re-rasterize all polygons and compute any      │
│       overlaps. If any overlap or mismatch remains, recompute polygons from  │
│       the authoritative masks and re-validate until there are zero overlaps  │
│       (or fail with non-zero exit code).                                     │
│  3 As a robust alternative, include an option to export authoritative masks  │
│    directly (RLE column or per-mask PNGs) as the canonical mask              │
│    representation — polygons can then be optional, derived later with        │
│    explicit guarantees.                                                      │
│  4 Run the script in the target runtime with real MobileSAM weights and real │
│    OpenCV/Pillow/pandas installed, and run the verification checks there:    │
│     • Confirm pairwise overlap count is zero                                 │
│     • Confirm each mask has only one connected component.                    │

│    between masks" is not met. I therefore cannot approve the solution as     │

│ from collections import deque                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_component_by_point(bin_mask, point=None): # bin_mask: boolean 2D │
│ array h, w = bin_mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=bool)    │
│ comps = []  # list of (size, pixels_set, contains_point)                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # neighbor offsets 4-connectivity                                           │
│  neigh = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  def in_bounds(r,c):                                                         │
│      return 0 &lt;= r &lt; h and 0 &lt;= c &lt; w                            │
│                                                                              │
│  # iterate through mask to find components                                   │
│  for r in range(h):                                                          │
│      for c in range(w):                                                      │
│          if bin_mask[r, c] and not visited[r, c]:                            │
│              q = deque()                                                     │
│              q.append((r,c))                                                 │
│              visited[r,c] = True                                             │
│              pixels = [(r,c)]                                                │
│              contains = False                                                │
│              while q:                                                        │
│                  y,x = q.popleft()                                           │
│                  if point is not None and (y == point[1] and x ==            │
│  point[0]):                                                                  │
│                      contains = True                                         │
│                  for dy,dx in neigh:                                         │
│                      ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx                                     │
│                      if in_bounds(ny,nx) and bin_mask[ny,nx] and not         │
│  visited[ny,nx]:                                                             │
│                          visited[ny,nx] = True                               │
│                          q.append((ny,nx))                                   │
│                          pixels.append((ny,nx))                              │
│              comps.append((len(pixels), pixels, contains))                   │
│                                                                              │
│  if not comps:                                                               │
│      return np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                          │
│  # if a component contains point, pick the first such (or largest among      │
│  those)                                                                      │
│  if point is not None:                                                       │
│      point_comps = [c for c in comps if c[2]]                                │
│      if point_comps:                                                         │
│          # build mask from the largest point-containing comp                 │
│          comp = max(point_comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                         │
│          out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│          for y,x in comp[1]:                                                 │
│              out[y,x] = 1                                                    │
│          return out                                                          │
│  # otherwise return the largest component                                    │
│  comp = max(comps, key=lambda x: x[0])                                       │
│  out = np.zeros_like(bin_mask, dtype=np.uint8)                               │
│  for y,x in comp[1]:                                                         │
│      out[y,x] = 1                                                            │
│  return out                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask): """Return polygon coordinates (xs, ys) for binary │
│ mask. Prefer to use cv2.findContours if available for better polygons.       │
│ Otherwise, a coarse bounding-box polygon is returned as fallback. """ # Try  │
│ OpenCV contour extraction first try: import cv2 mask_u8 =                    │
│ (mask.astype('uint8') * 255).astype('uint8') contours, _ =                   │
│ cv2.findContours(mask_u8, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) if       │
│ contours: contour = max(contours, key=lambda c: cv2.contourArea(c)) contour  │
│ = contour.squeeze() if contour.ndim == 1: contour = contour[np.newaxis, :]   │
│ xs = contour[:,0].astype(int).tolist() ys =                                  │
│ contour[:,1].astype(int).tolist()                                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│          # validate that rasterizing this polygon reproduces the mask        │
│  exactly                                                                     │
│          try:                                                                │
│              canvas = np.zeros_like(mask_u8)                                 │
│              pts = np.array([[xs[i], ys[i]] for i in range(len(xs))],        │
│  dtype=np.int32)                                                             │
│              pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2))                                     │
│              cv2.fillPoly(canvas, [pts], 255)                                │
│              # compare                                                       │
│              if np.array_equal((canvas&gt;0).astype(np.uint8),               │
│  mask.astype(np.uint8)):                                                     │
│                  return xs, ys                                               │
│              # otherwise fall through to robust edge-based contour           │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Robust fallback: construct polygon along exact pixel boundaries so that   │
│  # rasterizing the polygon reproduces the binary mask exactly.               │
│  h, w = mask.shape                                                           │
│  edges = {}                                                                  │
│  def add_edge(a,b):                                                          │
│      edges.setdefault(a, []).append(b)                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  # For each foreground pixel at (x,y) add boundary edges where neighbor is   │
│  background                                                                  │
│  for y in range(h):                                                          │
│      for x in range(w):                                                      │
│          if mask[y,x]:                                                       │
│              # top neighbor                                                  │
│              if y-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y-1,x]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  b = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # right neighbor                                                │
│              if x+1 &gt;= w or not mask[y,x+1]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y)                                                │
│                  b = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # bottom neighbor                                               │
│              if y+1 &gt;= h or not mask[y+1,x]:                              │
│                  a = (x+1, y+1)                                              │
│                  b = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│              # left neighbor                                                 │
│              if x-1 &lt; 0 or not mask[y,x-1]:                               │
│                  a = (x, y+1)                                                │
│                  b = (x, y)                                                  │
│                  add_edge(a,b)                                               │
│                  add_edge(b,a)                                               │
│                                                                              │
│  # chain edges into loops                                                    │
│  loops = []                                                                  │
│  visited_edges = set()                                                       │
│  for start in list(edges.keys()):                                            │
│      for nxt in list(edges.get(start, [])):                                  │
│          if (start,nxt) in visited_edges:                                    │
│              continue                                                        │
│          # walk                                                              │
│          loop = [start]                                                      │
│          cur = start                                                         │
│          prev = None                                                         │
│          while True:                                                         │
│              nbrs = edges.get(cur, [])                                       │
│              # pick next neighbor that&#x27;s not prev                       │
│              if not nbrs:                                                    │
│                  break                                                       │
│              # choose neighbor deterministically                             │
│              found = None                                                    │
│              for cand in nbrs:                                               │
│                  if cand == prev:                                            │
│                      continue                                                │
│                  found = cand                                                │
│                  break                                                       │
│              if found is None:                                               │
│                  break                                                       │
│              visited_edges.add((cur, found))                                 │
│              prev = cur                                                      │
│              cur = found                                                     │
│              if cur == loop[0]:                                              │
│                  break                                                       │
│              loop.append(cur)                                                │
│          if len(loop) &gt; 2:                                                │
│              loops.append(loop)                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  if not loops:                                                               │
│      # fallback bbox                                                         │
│      ys, xs = np.where(mask)                                                 │
│      if len(xs) == 0:                                                        │
│          return [], []                                                       │
│      xmin, xmax = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max())                               │
│      ymin, ymax = int(ys.min()), int(ys.max())                               │
│      return [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin], [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax]               │
│                                                                              │
│  # choose the outer loop (longest) as polygon                                │
│  outer = max(loops, key=lambda l: len(l))                                    │
│  xs = [p[0] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  ys = [p[1] for p in outer]                                                  │
│  return xs, ys                                                               │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ def clamp_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, w, h): xmin = int(max(0, min(w-1,     │
│ int(round(xmin))))) ymin = int(max(0, min(h-1, int(round(ymin))))) xmax =    │
│ int(max(0, min(w-1, int(round(xmax))))) ymax = int(max(0, min(h-1,           │
│ int(round(ymax))))) return xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax                            │
